lede: AI is rewriting luxury's discovery layer — from algorithms replacing clienteling to ChatGPT unlocking first-party audience targeting — while the BoF/McKinsey luxury client report confirms the channel shift is permanent and irreversible.

stories.headline: BoF × McKinsey: AI Algorithms Are Now Reshaping How Luxury Clients Discover, Compare and Decide — Brands Are Losing Control of the Relationship
stories.summary: Drawing on 2,000+ client surveys across the US and China, the BoF Insights/McKinsey 'Face to Face With Luxury Clients' report finds AI assistants are redefining the luxury shopping relationship — making behaviour more fluid, fragmented, and harder to influence through traditional brand channels. Luxury growth returns at 4–6% annually through 2030, but the brands that win will be those that learn to compete in AI-mediated discovery environments, not just boutiques. The report's AI findings land as a follow-on masterclass is scheduled for July 21 with BoF's Imran Amed and McKinsey's Gemma D'Auria.

stories.headline: ChatGPT Ads Unlock Audience Targeting and Custom Lists — OpenAI's Platform Is Now Structurally Closer to Google and Meta for Serious Advertisers
stories.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT advertising platform added audience targeting and custom first-party lists this week — moves that bring it closer to the targeting sophistication of Google and Meta. Advertisers can now upload customer email or phone lists under an 'Audiences' tag, while a separate update allows ChatGPT to generate AI-native ad creative for review and approval. The pace of feature rollout is accelerating faster than most media buyers can track, but platform glitches remain — including AI-mode citations routing clicks to competitor sites.

stories.headline: AI Millionaires Are Rewriting Luxury's Customer Map — And Maisons Are Not Built for Their Taste
stories.summary: A Reuters investigation (published July 8) reveals that a new cohort of AI-wealth millionaires — SpaceX shareholders, OpenAI early employees — is emerging as luxury's fastest-growing buyer segment in North America, but their preferences skew toward experiences, tech-integrated products, and smartwatches over traditional fashion and leather goods. LVMH, Richemont, Hermès and Kering all showed the Americas as their fastest-growing region in Q1 2026, driven partly by this wealth wave. The challenge: these buyers don't conform to heritage clienteling scripts, demanding a wholesale rethink of luxury's CRM and discovery models.

stories.headline: OpenAI Eyes $1 Trillion IPO Valuation With Advertising as a Core Revenue Pillar — Luxury Brands Are Already the Premium Target Audience
stories.summary: Forbes confirmed this week that OpenAI is targeting a Q4 2026 public debut at up to $1 trillion valuation, with advertising revenue — launched in January 2026 on free and Go-tier ChatGPT accounts — now a structural revenue pillar alongside subscriptions and API licensing. ChatGPT's 900 million weekly active users represent a premium intent-rich audience that luxury brands cannot afford to ignore, but reporting remains extremely limited with no demographic breakdown, audience insight or placement data. The IPO roadshow will force OpenAI to clarify the advertising product roadmap publicly for the first time.

stories.headline: Richemont Opens Luxury's H1 Reporting Season — Jewellery Dominates as Hard Luxury's Data-Driven Discipline Sets the Standard
stories.summary: Richemont is first out of the blocks in luxury's H1 2026 earnings cycle, setting the tone for results from LVMH and Kering later this month, according to BoF (July 12). The Swiss group's FY26 results — €22.4bn in sales, up 11% at constant rates — were underpinned by Jewellery Maisons outperforming across all regions, with the Americas and Middle East compensating for softer Asia-Pacific momentum. The results signal that data-disciplined, AI-assisted demand forecasting (Richemont's hallmark) is now a measurable competitive moat in hard luxury.
